correctness.rationale: The unique center is fixed under any automorphism. Its arms may only be permuted within length classes, and distance from the center fixes the position of each edge along an arm. The named colors are not exchanged. Independently enumerated interval cuts of m edges, keeping nondecreasing positive arm lengths with at least three parts. For each shape, enumerated all 2^m labeled edge masks, computed the unordered endpoint-pair path as XOR of the two center-route masks, and tallied (path length, number of ones) using bit counts. This gives exactly the two-component Parikh data, with multiplicity and no empty paths. Canonicalization by sorting arm words within equally long arms was cross-checked by the product of multiset counts. For edge counts 3…9 the row tuples (shapes, coloring classes, topology-scoped profiles, non-singleton fibers) are (1,4,4,0), (2,17,17,0), (4,66,66,0), (7,221,221,0), (11,688,688,0), (17,2034,2034,0), (25,5788,5786,2). The only ambiguous shape has distinct lengths (2,3,4), so all 512 of its labeled colorings are distinct modulo tree automorphism; its two exact doubletons match lines 10–11 and are swapped by complement. The direct profile in lines 52–56 matches the calculation with 45 endpoint pairs. No inference is made for topology-blind readout or larger spiders. value.rationale: Spiders are the simplest singly branching extension of paths, and fixed binary colors are the minimal nontrivial observation alphabet. The exact onset, unique obstructing shape and complete complement-paired fibers give minimal test instances and a finite identifiability boundary for the established small-unjumble problem, rather than another aggregate total.
